title: The naive framing: "does Claude remember?"
text: Someone assumed Claude already remembered their meetings for a daily briefing. It doesn't, it reads them fresh from what you type or connect every time. Does Claude read my meetings for a briefing? A skill is a folder Claude reads before

title: A skill is a folder
text: It works. This one is daily briefing, the skill. MD file holds the full instruction set in plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it then acts. The file is the program. The pipeline sits in the step section.

title: How the skill works
text: Claude reads each step in order then runs it. Linear, no branching unless a step says so. The scope is specific. Daily briefing

title: Standalone, or supercharged
text: Works stand-alone once you tell Claude your meetings and priorities in chat. Connect your calendar, CRM, and email and it's supercharged, reading them directly instead of waiting to be told. Either way, the same input produces the same briefing every time. Ask for something the file doesn't cover and the skill has nothing to say about it. Claude doesn't remember your day for a briefing. It reads what you give it,

title: Carry-out
text: Stand-alone or connected, and does the same thing with it every time. Your turn. Here's the prompt, read it with me. Read the daily briefing skill

title: Your turn
text: In this folder. Before you write my briefing, tell me exactly what you're using, what I told you versus what you need connected, and how you're ranking it before you do it. Claude daily briefing. Lay 'em in for bear.
